google-lakehouse-runtime-catalog:rest-sp.notes: The Iceberg REST catalog endpoint (biglake.googleapis.com/iceberg/v1/restcatalog) is the recommended interface, with an optional credential-vending mode for storage access delegation.
caveats: Iceberg v1 tables aren't supported and must be upgraded before use
Parquet data files only; the metadata.json file is limited to 1 MB
No fine-grained access control on tables managed through the REST endpoint
Custom write.data.path / write.metadata.path values are prohibited

google-lakehouse-runtime-catalog:v2-spec.notes: Iceberg v2 tables are generally available on the REST catalog endpoint.

google-lakehouse-runtime-catalog:v3-spec.notes: Iceberg v3 tables are supported in Preview on the REST catalog endpoint.
caveats: Pre-GA: v3 support is offered under Google Cloud's Pre-GA terms with limited support

google-lakehouse-runtime-catalog:managed.notes: Managed Lakehouse runtime catalog (formerly BigLake metastore, renamed April 2026; APIs and IAM still say biglake).

google-lakehouse-runtime-catalog:serves-.notes: Serves its own Iceberg tables over a spec-compliant Iceberg REST catalog endpoint with credential vending. Open-source engines (Spark, Flink, Trino) read and write runtime-catalog Iceberg tables at GA, including streaming writes, and since June 2026 BigQuery runs DDL/DML against the same tables (Preview). The BigQuery-managed (snapshot-export) Iceberg path is the read-only fallback, but IRC-native serving is now the primary, first-class path.
caveats: BigQuery-side DDL/DML on runtime-catalog tables is Preview; OSS engine read/write is GA

links.label: Use the BigLake metastore Iceberg REST catalog

google-lakehouse-runtime-catalog:rw-fore.notes: Foreign tables in remote IRC catalogs (Databricks Unity, AWS Glue, Snowflake Horizon) are reachable read-only through borderless / cross-cloud Lakehouse, which federates them into the runtime catalog over the Iceberg REST protocol and queries them from BigQuery or Spark without copying data. There is no write-back path to the foreign catalog, and the capability is Preview.
caveats: Read/query only: no write-back to the foreign catalog

google-lakehouse-runtime-catalog:federat.notes: Cross-cloud / borderless Lakehouse acts as a catalog-of-catalogs broker: it synchronizes metadata from remote Iceberg REST catalogs (Unity, Glue, Horizon) and SAP BDC into the runtime catalog so a single BigQuery or Spark session queries across them. Brokering is Preview (SAP BDC federation reached GA), so it is credited as partial rather than full.
caveats: Preview for the Unity/Glue/Horizon IRC brokers (SAP BDC federation is GA)

google-lakehouse-runtime-catalog:multi-e.notes: Multi-engine is GA (Spark, Flink, Hive, Trino and BigQuery share the same tables), but catalog-managed storage is GCS-only and multi-cloud reads go through BigQuery Omni external tables, not the IRC catalog.

google-lakehouse-runtime-catalog:governa.notes: No row-level security on managed Iceberg, and IRC-native tables have no fine-grained row/column access control either.
